candidates.name: Rental car
candidates.reason: Public transit + taxi fallback proven workable for all three stops; a self-drive car adds parking/navigation/driver-duty burden for 8 people and offers no accessibility benefit since Ginzan Onsen's town core is pedestrian-only regardless.

candidates.name: Notoya Ryokan
candidates.reason: Town's most iconic building and likely the hardest to book: online-only reservation system, phone/email/proxy bookings explicitly refused, and the ~3-month release window for Oct 20-23 dates has already passed as of the research date (2026-08-28).

candidates.name: Kosekiya Bekkan
candidates.reason: Only 30-guest capacity across 14 rooms — too small to comfortably host a single party of 8 alongside other guests without likely needing 2+ rooms split unpredictably.

candidates.name: Ryokan Matsumoto
candidates.reason: Best-documented booking policy (own FAQ) but online-only, no wheelchair-accessible rooms, and its own stated release window (1st of the month, 3 months ahead) for Oct 20-23, 2026 opened around 2026-08-01 — already passed by the time this research ran.

candidates.name: Mitoya
candidates.reason: Well-regarded local soba (2 min from Yamadera Station) but the official site states no group-capacity or reservation policy for a party of 8 — needs a direct phone call (023-695-2506) before it could be relied on.

candidates.name: Honogura Yamadera Honten
candidates.reason: Serves limited-quantity hand-made (juwari) soba on a scarcity model — not suited to a walk-in or reserved party of 8.

candidates.name: Yamagata Museum of Art
candidates.reason: Strong Western-art collection but not distinctly Yamagata history, and admission-charging — contradicts the off-the-beaten-path/local-history brief when free, more distinctive local options exist. Kept only as a wet-weather backup (see Day 2 plan_b).

candidates.name: Yamagata Prefectural Museum
candidates.reason: Generalist natural-history/prefecture museum, redundant with the more distinctive castle-era history sites already shortlisted in the same park.

candidates.name: Sobadokoro Shojiya
candidates.reason: Most-cited authentic local soba destination (155 years), but the official site gives no group-capacity info for a party of 8 — a same-name branch elsewhere does 20+ groups; call 023-622-1380 to confirm before booking.

candidates.name: Suzuki Sohonten
candidates.reason: Offers group soba-kaiseki courses but exact seating capacity was not found in any source — needs a direct call (023-622-5636) before relying on it.

candidates.name: Inokoya Yamagatada
candidates.reason: Thematically ideal (imoni served year-round in individual mini-hearth pots, 1 min from the station) but private rooms seat only 4-6 with curtain dividers — an 8-top would need open floor seating, not a private room. Fine as a casual/overflow stop, not the flagship group meal.

candidates.name: Cold niku-soba
candidates.reason: The dish's true home is Kahoku town, a separate excursion outside the trip's three cities — noted as a genuine regional specialty but out of scope for this itinerary.

evidence.claim: One-way adult fare Oishida Station → Ginzan Onsen is ¥1,000 (¥500 child/disabled companion), cash only — the fare box does not accept IC cards
The Ginzan Line's 2026 regular-season operating window is April 1 – October 24, 2026 — this covers the entire Oct 20-23, 2026 trip, ending the day after departure
No reservation is required on the Ginzan Line bus; it is explicitly listed as EXEMPT from the town's day-tripper ticket/entry-restriction system
5-6 daily round trips; sample Oishida→Ginzan departures 6:40/9:57/12:42/14:17/16:02/17:52, and Ginzan→Oishida returns 7:15/8:54/11:04/13:54/15:24/17:04

Ginzan Onsen's private-vehicle demonstration restriction project concluded March 1, 2026, with no announced resumption as of the research date — route buses, delivery vehicles, and overnight guests' designated ryokan parking remain exempt regardless of any future restriction
The prior winter 2025-26 restriction period ran Dec 20, 2025 – Mar 1, 2026, park-and-ride only for day-trippers; overnight guests were exempt throughout
13 ryokan are listed on the town's official lodging directory, with capacities ranging from ~12 to ~200 guests
Ginzanso is the largest property in Ginzan Onsen — 40 rooms, ~200 guest capacity — the best single-property fit for hosting a group of 8

Ryokan Matsumoto accepts reservations only online (official site, Rakuten Travel, or Jalan) — phone and email reservations are not accepted; bookings open at the start of the month, 3 months ahead of the stay date
Ryokan Matsumoto has an elevator but no wheelchair-accessible (barrier-free) guest rooms, per its own FAQ
Ryokan Matsumoto allows guests to mail luggage ahead (food items excluded; oversized items need advance email notice)
Notoya Ryokan accepts reservations online only — phone/email reservations and third-party (proxy) bookings are explicitly refused, for both domestic and international guests
Risshaku-ji (Yamadera) adult admission is ¥500 (middle-school age and up), revised from ¥300 effective April 1, 2025 — many aggregators still show the stale ¥300 figure
Risshaku-ji reception hours are 8:00-16:00 (Apr-Sep bracket, which covers Oct 20-23) and 8:30-15:00 in winter (Dec-Mar); cash only for admission

The only route from the base entrance to the upper halls (Godaido, Okunoin) is on foot via ~1,015 stone steps; the temple's own access page describes no mechanized assist, and no funicular/ropeway/shortcut exists anywhere on the mountain
Step count base-to-Okunoin is cited as 1,015 steps by Yamagata Prefecture's own tourism site
The local Yamadera tourism-association site cites 1,070 steps for the same climb — a minor counting-convention discrepancy from the prefecture's 1,015 figure, not materially different for planning
Konponchudo (the main hall, ~3 min walk from the base entrance) is a genuinely worthwhile visit without climbing the stairway — the one legitimate low-effort option at Yamadera

A firsthand account from a visitor with impaired leg function found even the base/lower precinct near Konponchudo has enough steps and unevenness to be genuinely hard to navigate, and confirmed Yamadera has no ramps or elevators — there is no easy half-experience of the mountain beyond the base

Yamadera is least crowded right at the 8:00 opening and on weekdays (Tue-Thu); 10:00-14:00 is the most crowded window as tour groups arrive, worse still in koyo season when buses start building by 8:00-10:00
A independent photography-focused visitor blog corroborates arriving 8:00-9:00am to avoid overwhelming daytime crowds and a packed Godaido viewing platform
Mitoya's official site (2 min from Yamadera Station, hand-made local soba) does not state a group capacity or reservation policy for parties of 8
Kajo Park is free, open 5:00-22:00 (Apr-Oct) / 5:30-22:00 (Nov-Mar), never fully closed; 230 free parking spaces
Bunshokan: hours 9:00-16:30, free admission, address Hatago-cho 3-4-51, Yamagata city, closed 1st/3rd Mondays

Bunshokan's former assembly hall chamber was closed for construction with a stated target of reopening by end of September 2026 — a deadline, not a confirmed reopening; re-verify closer to the Oct 2026 trip that it actually reopened on schedule

The restored Otemon Yagura gate-tower is confirmed open to the public by Yamagata city's own page, which points to a separate page for exact hours; no accessibility information (stairs vs. elevator) is stated — treat as a likely skip for the 2 low-mobility travelers pending direct confirmation
Kyu-Saiseikan (former Meiji-era hospital, octagonal 3-tier building, Yamagata City Folk Museum) hours 9:00-16:30, free admission since Apr 1, 2009, closed Dec 29-Jan 3
Mogami Yoshiaki Historical Museum hours 9:00-17:00 (last entry 16:30), free admission since Apr 1, 2009, closed Mondays and certain holidays, address Otemachi 1-53, phone 023-625-7101

Yamagata Museum of Art hours 10:00-17:00, adult admission ¥800 (¥640 for groups of 20+), closed Mondays — sourced from a subagent's search-preview; two of my own direct WebFetch attempts to the museum's own site failed with a connection error (not a 403 block, the domain itself appears unreachable from this environment), so this ships with a confirm-ahead flag

Beninokura (山形市十日町2-1-8) is a tourist complex ≈10 min walk from JR Yamagata Station (or a 100-yen loop bus), offering local food, regional products, farm-direct sales of traditional vegetables, and a 100-yen sake-tasting vending machine
Soba Sanbyakubou's private storehouse room (蔵座敷) seats up to 30 for dining/banquets; hours 11:00-20:00 (last order 19:30), closed Mondays

Yonezawa Beef Tokiwa (Yamagata store) has 4 private rooms seating up to 14 guests; minimum spend ¥6,600/person lunch, ¥9,900/person dinner; hours 11:00-22:00 (last order 21:00); reservable by phone (023-666-4433) or online (TableCheck); address Sachimachi 2-9, ground floor of the Daiwa Roynet Hotel by the station

The Nihon-ichi Imonikai Festival 2026 (Japan's largest imoni-stew festival) is confirmed for Sunday September 20, 2026 at the Mogami riverbed near Sougetsu Bridge — this falls BEFORE the Oct 20-23 trip window and does not overlap; imoni remains available year-round at restaurants regardless, and October is peak taro-harvest season locally

US passport holders qualify for Japan's general visa-exemption framework (tourism stays, no ETA/JESTA requirement in force for 2026 — the proposed pre-clearance system targets FY2028 launch at the earliest); exact stay length (commonly cited as 90 days) is published on MOFA's own exemption table, which could not be directly fetched in this research session (repeated 403s) — this is the single best-available official-adjacent corroboration and should be re-checked against mofa.go.jp before booking. ASSUMES a US passport — the traveler party's passport countries were not stated in intake.

US State Department travel advisory for Japan is Level 1 — Exercise Normal Precautions; the primary page (travel.state.gov) is Cloudflare-gated and returned HTTP 403 on every direct fetch attempt in this session (no embedded-browser tool available) — recorded honestly as blocked, corroborated only by convergent search-result snippets and the OSAC page title; a human should re-confirm directly on travel.state.gov before the guide ships

Ginzan Onsen has no convenience store and no ATM in the town itself (nearest is ~30 min by car); several ryokan there are cash-only (no credit card / QR pay) — carry sufficient cash before heading there
The gas lamps along Ginzan Onsen's main street begin lighting around 16:00, with the best photo window 16:30-17:30 into blue hour, fully dark by 18:00, lamps off around 21:00

Ginzan Onsen's worst crowding is around midday (~12:00); the photogenic evening lamp-lit window (17:00-20:00) is also the most crowded time of day, while before 11:00 or after 14:00 daytime is comparatively calm
A second independent blog corroborates the midday-worst / evening-photogenic-but-crowded crowd pattern at Ginzan Onsen

The path to Shirogane Falls at the end of Ginzan Onsen's main street involves an uphill stairway described by local sources as 'fairly tough' — roughly 6 minutes' walk; this is a real mobility consideration distinct from the flat riverside main street where the ashiyu foot bath sits

Ginzan Onsen's main attractions: the Taisho-era wooden ryokan street along the Ginzan River, gas lamps, Shirogane Falls (22m) at the street's end, the riverside 'Waraku' ashiyu foot bath, and rentable period costumes

In 2025, Yamadera/Yamagata-area koyo (autumn foliage) illumination ran Oct 26 - Nov 9; the Oct 20-23, 2026 trip dates fall roughly 1-2 weeks BEFORE that typical peak/illumination window — trees will likely be just beginning to turn rather than at full peak. This is an inference from the most recent comparable season, not a confirmed 2026 forecast (2026 forecasts are not published until September 2026) — re-check tenki.jp or weathernews.jp/koyo closer to the trip

Visible tattoos are not illegal in Japan; onsen tattoo restrictions are facility-specific policy rather than a nationwide legal requirement, and many traditional ryokan still restrict them for cultural reasons — a private/family bath (kashikiri-buro) reservation is the standard workaround. Not individually confirmed for any specific Ginzan Onsen ryokan this pass.
The only Japanese public holiday in October 2026 is Sports Day on Oct 12 (a Monday) — nothing falls in the Oct 20-23 trip window

reservations.actionDate: 2026-08-29 — book immediately; today's date (2026-08-28) is already inside or past the typical release window most Ginzan Onsen ryokan use for Oct 20-23, 2026 dates
reservations.partyRules: Largest property in town (40 rooms / ~200 guests) — best odds of hosting all 8 in one property without a split, but exact single-booking group-size limits were not confirmed; call 0237-28-2322 to arrange a group booking directly
reservations.deposit: Not confirmed this pass — ask when booking
reservations.cancellation: Not confirmed this pass — ask when booking
reservations.foreignFriction: Not confirmed this pass; Ginzan Onsen ryokan bookings commonly run through Rakuten Travel/Jalan (English-friendly) or direct phone (Japanese)
reservations.walkIn: No — Ginzan Onsen ryokan do not take walk-in overnight guests during peak season

leads.claim: Concierge or travel-agency package booking may secure a room even after the standard release window closes, per general Japanese ryokan booking practice

reservations.alternatives: Takimikan (18 rooms/70 guests, has a 50-seat banquet hall) or Showakan (13 rooms/50 guests) as single-property backups; a 2-property split (e.g. Takimikan + Showakan) as a last resort
reservations.fallback: If no Ginzan Onsen ryokan can seat all 8 for these exact dates, fall back to splitting the group across 2 adjacent properties, or shifting the overnight to Yamagata city and treating Ginzan Onsen as a long day trip instead (loses the signature evening lamp-lit stay but keeps the itinerary intact)

reservations.releaseWindow: Not stated as a hard window; TableCheck online booking is available for standard advance reservation, no evidence of a strict release date
reservations.actionDate: Book 1-2 weeks ahead once the exact day is fixed, given the party of 8 needs a private room (4 rooms available, max 14 each)
reservations.partyRules: Private rooms seat up to 14 — comfortably fits 8; minimum spend ¥6,600/person lunch or ¥9,900/person dinner applies
reservations.deposit: Not separately confirmed; the per-person minimum spend functions as the binding commitment
reservations.cancellation: Not confirmed this pass — ask when booking
reservations.foreignFriction: TableCheck's interface may default to Japanese; phone booking (023-666-4433) or the site's email inquiry form are alternatives if the online system is awkward
reservations.walkIn: Possible outside peak times but risky for a party of 8 wanting a private room — reserve ahead
reservations.alternatives: Soba Sanbyakubou at Beninokura (confirmed 30-seat private storehouse room) as the second flagship group meal
reservations.fallback: Open floor seating at the same restaurant, or shift the group dinner to Soba Sanbyakubou

transport.route: Oishida Station → Ginzan Onsen (Hanagasa Bus, Ginzan Line) — the trip's anchor transfer, carried with luggage
transport.doorToDoor: Yamagata city hotel → Yamagata Station (local Ou Line ~50 min or Tsubasa ~28 min to Oishida) → Hanagasa Bus (~35-40 min) → Ginzan Onsen. Total door-to-door roughly 1-1.5 hours depending on train choice and connection wait.
transport.transferReality: Oishida Station has no confirmed step-free path to the bus stop and no IC card acceptance (cash ticket required); the bus stop sits just outside the station. Not independently confirmed as fully barrier-free — worth a direct check for the 2 low-mobility travelers.
transport.groupLuggageMobility: The Ginzan Line bus is a small retro coach with no stated luggage-space limit found in this research; boarding early/first at Oishida is the practical mitigation for 8 people with bags. If the bus is visibly full or luggage won't fit, 2-3 taxis are the fallback (see c-chartered-taxi--oishida-ginzan-onsen).
transport.buffer: Recommend the mid-morning or early-afternoon departure (12:42 or 14:17 from Oishida) rather than the first slot, to allow an unhurried hotel checkout and train connection without a tight transfer window.
transport.missedConnection: Missing a bus means waiting roughly 1.5-2.5 hours for the next one — only 5-6 buses run per day and there is no rail alternative into Ginzan Onsen.
transport.lastPracticalReturn: 17:04 departing Ginzan Onsen is the last bus back to Oishida — relevant to the return/departure leg, not the inbound trip with luggage.
transport.fallback: Chartered taxi from Oishida Station (~20 min, roughly ¥6,500-8,000 per car per an independent fare-estimator site, 2-3 cars needed for 8 people + luggage) — call Ōbanazawa Taxi (0237-23-2525) ahead given a limited local fleet. A taxi directly from Yamagata city (~51 min drive) is a further fallback if the Oishida connection is missed entirely.

transport.doorToDoor: Tokyo Station to Yamagata Station, roughly 2h22m (fastest) to 2h45-55m depending on the specific service, hourly-ish frequency, ~06:12-20:44 daily window per an independent rail-fare aggregator (not independently confirmed against JR East's own timetable — bot-gated in this session).
transport.groupLuggageMobility: No mandatory oversized-baggage reservation applies on this Shinkansen network (unlike Tokaido/Sanyo/Kyushu); storage is first-come, first-served overhead/behind-seat space — book all 8 seats together to keep the group's bags near their own seats.
transport.missedConnection: Roughly hourly service — a missed train costs about an hour's wait, not a lost day.
transport.fallback: Board at Ueno or Omiya instead of Tokyo Station if more convenient — the same physical train (coupled Yamabiko+Tsubasa) calls at both.

disagreements.topic: Whether a seasonal private-vehicle restriction applies to Ginzan Onsen during the Oct 2026 trip window
disagreements.investigation: Initial research (via a subagent) found a documented winter 2025-26 restriction period (Dec 20, 2025 - Mar 1, 2026) and flagged that 2026 autumn restriction dates were not yet published, treating a possible autumn restriction as a live open question for the Oct 2026 trip. A direct fetch of the SAME official page (ginzan-artmuseum.com/regulated-vehicles/) later in this same research pass found current text stating the whole private-vehicle demonstration-restriction project concluded March 1, 2026, with no announced resumption.
disagreements.resolution: Resolved in favor of the more current, directly-fetched page: no vehicle restriction is expected to apply to Ginzan Onsen for the Oct 20-23, 2026 trip. This doesn't change the transport recommendation (bus/taxi over rental car, since the town core is pedestrian-only regardless and public transit is already proven workable) but removes a previously-flagged access risk from the plan.

disagreements.topic: Exact step count for the Yamadera (Risshaku-ji) climb
disagreements.investigation: Yamagata Prefecture's own tourism site cites 1,015 steps; the local Yamadera tourism-association site cites 1,070 — likely a different counting start-point or convention.
disagreements.resolution: Treated as materially the same for trip planning (~1,000-1,070 steps); the prefecture's own figure (1,015) is used as the headline number since it is the more authoritative of the two.

saturation.note: Five parallel research threads (Ginzan Onsen transfer/lodging, Yamadera, Yamagata city sights/food, practical essentials, Tokyo-Yamagata transit) plus direct follow-up fetches converged on a stable set of picks: later searches for additional restaurant/lodging candidates (e.g. Hanazen, Yamagata Nagaya Sakaba, further soba shops) returned weaker or capacity-unconfirmed options that would not displace the shipped picks. The one genuinely open uncertainty — whether Ginzanso (or any Ginzan Onsen ryokan) still has live availability for Oct 20-23, 2026 given the release-window risk found — is NOT resolvable by further web research; it requires a real-time booking action, which is why it is handled via the reservations[] action date, a shipped fallback plan (split across 2 properties, or convert Ginzan Onsen to a day trip), and a traveler question card rather than more searching. Environment note: this session had no shell/script access (lookup-place.mjs, lookup-venue.mjs, lookup-tz.mjs, search-commons.mjs were unavailable), and several primary domains were persistently bot-gated (jreast.co.jp, mofa.go.jp, travel.state.gov, jp.usembassy.gov, osac.gov — all returned HTTP 403 across repeated direct attempts by multiple independent fetches) — those gaps are recorded honestly per-fact (blocked access, confirm-ahead flags) rather than silently upgraded to clean citations.
